### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73c9ae4f0fb89320fac7444690e239423ad593cd` — the merge of head `55f3d0a800bfc04477738a3b1627bb2eaf4cf28e` into base `836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73c9ae4f0fb89320fac7444690e239423ad593cd && git checkout 73c9ae4f0fb89320fac7444690e239423ad593cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3 55f3d0a800bfc04477738a3b1627bb2eaf4cf28e && git checkout -B drift-repro 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3 && git merge --no-ff 55f3d0a800bfc04477738a3b1627bb2eaf4cf28e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 90/90 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55f3d0a800bfc04477738a3b1627bb2eaf4cf28e`

### ① Derived judgments

1. **False refusals — none found.**
   - The rule refuses only the `traversals` that `analyzeRelationshipTraversals(source, root)` reports, for the roots `record` / `previous` / `parent`, and only when the first hop is typed in `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` = `lookup, master_detail, user, tree` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts:154`).
   - `packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts` (unchanged against `origin/main`) files a value use in `bareFields`, not `traversals`. That covers `record.REF == 'id'`, `record.REF != null`, `has(record.REF)` and a method receiver; its own test pins `"record.name.startsWith('A')"` → `traversals.size` 0.
   - `current_user.*`, including `can(...)`, is never analysed. An `address`-typed `record.ship_to.city` is skipped. The multi-hop `record.REF.a.b` is refused, not missed.
2. **False acceptances — all in the safe direction, none inside the card's three slots over declared fields:**
   - (a) a read through an injected column (`owner_id`, `created_by`), which the lint type index does not type (declared by the PR);
   - (b) `parent.REF.COL` when the master is not in the stack, or when the object has other than one `master_detail`;
   - (c) a computed receiver (a deliberate limit, stated in the analyzer's docblock);
   - (d) field-level `visibleWhen` and form-view / action-param option `visibleWhen`, which are outside triage's point 2.
3. **Doors and severity — reached, at `error`.**
   - `authoring-rules.ts:460-513`: `validateStackExpressions` is `tier: 'gating'` and `commands: ALL`.
   - It is called from `validate.ts:349`, `compile.ts:399` and `lint.ts:673`.
   - The runtime-door claim is TRUE: `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'action', 'hook']`.
4. **Sentence truth — every sentence checked is TRUE.**
   - Option: `evaluateOptionVisibility` (`rule-validator.ts:2957-3001`) does `continue; // fail-open` on `!res.ok`, and the D2 docblock (`:185-186`) says option visibility 「stays fail-open」.
   - `previous.`: `:3910-3912` reads 「the `previous` root is never hydrated」.
   - `parent.`: bound only for field `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen`, as a plain `findOne` of the stored master.
   - The prescription is byte-equal to `unevaluableFieldRuleError` (`:3675-3676`), and the quoted runtime text exists (`:3615`).
   - The regenerated `field` / `object` / `migration` / `view` reference pages carry the new sentences.
5. **ADR-0087 route right; the registry is generated.**
   - No conversion exists (turning a predicate into a failure-condition rule is a judgment), so a D3 semantic entry is the structured TODO. It is the route ADR-0137 D1 itself took (`0137:127`).
   - The entry sits at `registry.ts:8601`, inside the generated `semantic:18` markers. The entry file and the registry block are identical after the indent is stripped.
6. **Nothing pinned the old acceptance.** `git grep` at head over `examples/**`, `packages/platform-objects/**`, `skills/**` and `content/docs/**`: every `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen` reads an own column or `parent.status`, and no option `visibleWhen` traverses.
7. **CI at head:** 28 success, 5 skipped, 0 failure at review time. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 at `836aad2a`.

### ② Semver level
Conformant:
- `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, the `fix(lint)!:` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner, the `adr-0087: registered` marker, and `Clause-②: no`.
- `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` in the launch window, and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:634` reads `bang` from the `!:` summary.
- `no` is truthful: nothing widens.
- The CLI change is test-only, so no changeset is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Clause-② arm: accepted as written. The fuller spelling would be `no (narrowing)`.
- Runtime wording for `previous` / `parent`: true. It is `domain:engine`, unreachable by metadata that passes lint, and correctly not filed here.
- Stored objects not re-judged at the runtime object-write door: pre-existing scoping, outside remedy A.
- Coverage boundary: true, and in the safe direction.
- Shared describe: `view.mdx` renders the scoped sentence.
- Not merged with main: verified clean with `merge-tree`, and no registry entry is adjacent.
